sections_checked: definition and comparison to worst-case differential privacy
two simulation examples and empirical limitations

title: A privacy-preserving system for data ownership using blockchain and distributed databases
review_status: full-text audit complete after retry; architecture/prototype described, but no quantified privacy attack, formal proof, scalability measurement, or field evaluation reported
sections_checked: §II proposed ownership, trust, and data-separation assumptions
§III architecture: decentralized plaintext user-data store, identity databases, blockchain/SSI
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2018-10-27; no venue publication verified
evidence_note: Full v1 PDF (8 pages) retrieved and extracted. Prototype stack is BigchainDB, MongoDB, private Ethereum node, and uPort. User-data records are stored in plaintext but described as de-identified; access is mediated through role-based APIs and identity fields are held separately. The paper discusses student/medical use cases but reports no quantified re-identification attack, formal privacy proof, performance/scaling benchmark, or field evaluation. This is an architecture proposal/prototype, not measured evidence of protection at scale.

title: Towards Deploying a Scalable & Robust Vehicular Identity and Credential Management Infrastructure
review_status: full-text audit complete; 10,000-emulated-client controlled evaluation and protocol-security/privacy design checked; network propagation and vehicle key generation are outside reported provisioning latency
sections_checked: comparison/future-work statements on omitted network propagation
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2016-01-05; no later venue claim asserted in this audit
evidence_note: Controlled virtualized setup emulates 10,000 vehicle clients and reports around 500 ms to obtain 100 pseudonyms; reports four-fold speedup over prior systems under similar setup. Network delay was intentionally eliminated and vehicle-side key generation excluded. Full PDF and extracted text checked; operational claim is bounded to this testbed.

title: Assessing the Privacy Cost in Centralized Event-Based Demand Response for Microgrids
review_status: full-text audit complete; formal cost definition, 4-bus simulated feeder, scenario design, privacy/optimality results, and transfer limitations checked
sections_checked: §V simulation setup, customer scenarios, Figures 2–5 and numerical discussion
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 posted 2017; no venue claim asserted in this audit
evidence_note: Simulation uses an 8.7-MVA 4-bus feeder model, 4-MVA generation and up to 1,500 simulated customers. One mixed-customer case reports cost 0.59 at ε=1 and ~0.63 at ε=0.1; some homogeneous-privacy cases approach 1, while a heterogeneous setting is around 0.4. This is not field-measured and is conditional on the objective, feeder, synthetic demand/utilities, and Laplace mechanism.

title: Towards Measuring Membership Privacy
review_status: full-text audit complete; DTP/PDTP definitions, three attack evaluation, per-record counterexample, correlation statistics, and training-stability limitations checked
sections_checked: §§2–4 threat model, attack definitions, DTP/PDTP metrics
§5.1–5.4 datasets, classifiers, attack protocols and metrics
§6 training stability, Table 3, and known classifier conditions
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2017-12-25; no venue publication asserted in this audit
evidence_note: On NN-Purchase, attack accuracies are 0.6680, 0.6257, and 0.8533; PDTP correlations with those attacks are 0.4864, 0.5052, and 0.7653. Correlation with maximum per-record accuracy over the three attacks is 0.8936. One record has distance-based attack at baseline and untargeted accuracy 0.94. DTP can require all-query search; PDTP is a relaxation, and training stability is unknown for several tested model families.
